quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, what will most likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and get a ticket.
You will improve traffic flow.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you stop the normal flow of traffic by driving too slowly, you can get a ticket. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, unless that speed is over the legal limit.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic light?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Come to a complete stop.
You can turn left after you let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right of way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn left after you let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving techniques to prevent crashes.
Riskier than regular driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving techniques to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe techniques to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
Stay until police arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When your vehicle will not fit completely across the tracks.
In towns with frequent trains.
When carrying two or more children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle will not fit completely across the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time. Do not start crossing unless you can clear the tracks completely. Never stop your car on the tracks.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you know?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires slip more easily, so slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires slip more easily, so slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires do not grip gravel and dirt as well as pavement. Slow down on these roads. Your car will take longer to stop and will skid more easily when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns you of a sharp turn and tells you to reduce speed.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this warning sign tell you?

options.text: An intersection ahead.
A crosswalk ahead.
A railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is coming. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What word appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A red octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If power steering stops working, you will need extra effort to steer. Slow down and drive to a safe area off the road to stop.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is moving at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, if an approaching train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle won't damage the gate.
Yes, if you look carefully both ways.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive so slowly that you block normal traffic, you can be cited.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have little protection, so do not crowd them. Passing too quickly can push them off course.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are fully up and all warning signals have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when a green light or green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when a green light or green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before moving.
